newsitem.title: RUSSIA: GM to start Blazer output in Russia in Dec.
newsitem.headline: GM to start Blazer output in Russia in Dec.

text.p: U.S. automaker General Motors Corp said on Tuesday it would start building the Chevrolet Blazer, a GM sport utility vehicle, in December in a joint venture in an autonomous part of Russia.
"We will start producing Blazers in Russia next month," George Baker, vice president of General Motors Overseas Distribution Corp, told Reuters.

"It's going to begin with limited assembly on small scale, gradually growing to 250 units a month. Our ultimate objective is to reach 4,500 units a month at the end of two years, so we can achieve our goal of producing 50,000 units annually."

The joint venture, located roughly 1,400 kilometres east of Moscow, was formed in December 1995 with Elabuga Avtomobilny Zavod (ElAZ), an enterprise majority owned by the government in Tartarstan, a self-governing region in Russia.
The venture, owned 75 percent by ElAZ and 25 percent by GM, plans to invest as much as $250 million in the plant.
As the volume of production increases, the plant will install equipment and facilities to broaden the scope of its assembly functions, Baker said.
"We will construct a world-class paint booth, but it will take 20 to 24 months to complete," he said.
GM has said the project plans to source as much as 25 percent of the value of the Blazers from Russia and Baker said Russian truckmaker AO KamAZ would help tool the plant.
"KamAZ is going to provide us with a significant amount of spare parts and metal stamping," Baker said.
